data.title: Grove outlines $142.5M-$152.5M 2026 net revenue outlook while leaning into Amazon and dropship expansion
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Grove Collaborative Holdings, Inc. (GROV) Q2 2026

Management View

  • Jeff Yurcisin (CEO, President & Director) said the quarter matched the company’s “revenue trough” framing from last quarter, stating, “Net revenue grew 1% sequentially to $36.6 million.” He highlighted profitability and cash generation: “Adjusted EBITDA was $0.5 million, our third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. And operating cash flow was positive $1.3 million.”
  • Yurcisin emphasized monetization levers tied to customer experience and fulfillment, including “an updated subscription experience” and “efficiencies from our updated outbound shipping strategy, which improved our outbound shipping costs in the second quarter.”
  • Yurcisin positioned channel mix as a near-term growth driver, noting, “D2C revenue declined slightly quarter-over-quarter, while total net revenue grew, driven by growth in our non-D2C channels, including Amazon and QVC.” He added that the company is “expanding our own brand business without cannibalizing our DTC platform,” while also saying, “It’s still early, and we’re watching closely to make sure this is additive to the business.”
  • Yurcisin introduced a new assortment expansion mechanism, saying, “We recently launched dropship capabilities,” adding it “lets us further expand selection into new categories without the inventory ownership costs.” He said the company launched “with two brands this past week,” and plans to move into “mattresses and air filtration and water purification systems.”
  • Yurcisin disclosed a leadership change: “As previously disclosed, Tom will be leaving Grove on August 16th to pursue a new opportunity,” and added, “Our search for a successor is underway.”
  • Tom Siragusa (CFO, Principal Financial Officer & Principal Accounting Officer) framed performance versus expectations: “Our results this quarter are consistent with the outlook we provided last quarter,” and added, “We grew revenue sequentially. We continue to see improvements in unit economics.”

Outlook

  • Siragusa reaffirmed full-year targets: “For full year 2026, we continue to expect net revenue of $142.5 million to $152.5 million and adjusted EBITDA to be positive low single-digit millions.”
  • He reiterated cadence expectations: “We still expect sequential revenue improvement in each remaining quarter in 2026.”
  • Compared with last quarter, the company’s Q2 message was described as maintaining the higher outlook already set in Q1, with Siragusa saying, “we are reaffirming the top and bottom line guidance we raised during the first quarter.”
  • The provided analysts estimates data was not usable for comparisons in this section because it did not include revenue estimates and used a fiscal quarter format that did not match the required Q1–Q4 convention.

Financial Results

  • Grove reported Q2 net revenue of $36.6 million (down 16.9% year-over-year, up 1% quarter-over-quarter), with Siragusa attributing the year-over-year pressure to “a smaller active customer base entering the year,” tied to “lower advertising investment” and “customer attrition tied to the e-commerce platform disruption throughout 2025.”
  • Customer and order metrics remained pressured: “DTC total orders were 489,000,” and “Active customers totaled 509,000 at quarter end.” Siragusa also reported DTC net revenue per order of “$69.19.”
  • Margin and earnings detail included a gross margin decline to “53.6%,” which Siragusa said was “primarily driven by one-time disposals in the quarter,” partially offset by “a more targeted promotional strategy.” Net loss was “$0.9 million,” while adjusted EBITDA was “positive $0.5 million.”
  • Expense and cash items emphasized structural cost actions and working capital: Siragusa reported SG&A of “$17.6 million,” cash of “$11.4 million,” and operating cash flow “positive $1.3 million,” driven by “a decrease in inventory.”

Q&A

  • No analyst Q&A session was included in this transcript; the call content provided consisted of prepared remarks.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: No analyst questions were provided in the Q2 transcript, preventing a direct read on analyst tone this quarter.
  • Management: Prepared remarks were steady and execution-focused, with Yurcisin stating, “we’re clear-eyed that our revenue is still down year-over-year and that re-accelerating it remains the work in front of us,” alongside confidence language such as, “That’s what gives me confidence in the path forward.”
  • Versus Q1, management’s tone remained focused on sequential improvement, but Q2 added a notable transition point with the CFO departure announcement (“Tom will be leaving Grove on August 16th”).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Strategy emphasis shifted from Q1’s heavy focus on platform recovery and “green shoots” to Q2’s operational scaling levers, including “dropship capabilities” and explicitly leaning into Amazon as “part of our second half strategy.”
  • Guidance direction differed in action but not endpoint: Q1 raised full-year guidance, while Q2 “reaffirm[ed]” the raised ranges and repeated expectations for “sequential revenue improvement in each remaining quarter in 2026.”
  • Key business momentum markers moved from Q1’s mobile app stabilization and cohort recovery to Q2’s subscription update delivery (“we delivered a meaningfully improved subscription experience during the second quarter”) and non-DTC contribution (Amazon/QVC).
  • Analyst focus cannot be compared because Q2 did not include Q&A; Q1’s Q&A included questions on performance drivers, gross margin durability, loyalty adoption, and tariffs.

Risks and Concerns

  • Revenue risk remained explicit: Yurcisin said, “our revenue is still down year-over-year and that re-accelerating it remains the work in front of us.”
  • Customer base and demand-generation risk persisted, with Siragusa citing “a smaller active customer base entering the year” and the “compounding effects of lower advertising investment.”
  • Gross margin variability was highlighted through “one-time disposals in the quarter,” and the company also signaled future spend increases: “we expect to grow our advertising investment with discipline in future quarters.”
  • Channel strategy risk management was acknowledged in Amazon expansion: “we’re watching closely to make sure this is additive to the business.”
  • Leadership transition risk was introduced with the CFO departure and an ongoing succession process: “Our search for a successor is underway.”

Final Takeaway

Management presented Q2 as execution against a stabilization plan—$36.6 million of net revenue with sequential growth, a third straight quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA, and positive operating cash flow—while reiterating full-year 2026 guidance of $142.5 million to $152.5 million in net revenue and adjusted EBITDA in the “positive low single-digit millions.” The company emphasized that re-accelerating growth remains the priority, pointing to an updated subscription experience, planned disciplined increases in advertising, expansion in non-DTC channels including Amazon, and a new dropship model to broaden assortment without traditional inventory ownership, alongside disclosure that CFO Tom Siragusa will depart on August 16 and a successor search is in progress.

data.title: These materials stocks pair A+ momentum with stretched valuations
data.description:
Wall Street investors are increasingly seeking refuge in high-performing equity plays as volatile materials markets continue to shift, forcing a critical evaluation of stock price velocity against fundamental underlying valuations.

Analysts warn that chasing recent momentum can leave market participants overexposed to highly priced assets, prompting a rush toward selective screens that highlight cheap high flyers within the specialty chemicals, steel, aluminum, and mining sectors.

Below is a list of the top 10 materials stocks with top momentum grades that are widely regarded as cheap high flyer stocks. Each of these stocks is listed according to its highest momentum grade along with its valuation grade, representing companies in the specialty chemicals, steel, aluminum, and mining industries.

The list is topped by Aspen Aerogels, Inc. (ASPN), with a momentum grade of A+ and valuation grade of C-. Flotek Industries, Inc. (FTK) and Kaiser Aluminum Corporation (KALU) follow closely behind, both carrying perfect A+ momentum ratings.

Koppers Holdings Inc. (KOP), Materion Corporation (MTRN), and Myers Industries, Inc. (MYE) round out the middle of the pack, while steel giants Nucor Corporation (NUE) and Steel Dynamics, Inc. (STLD) also make the top 10. Perimeter Solutions, Inc. (PRM) and Suncrete, Inc. (RMIX) complete the list of high-momentum materials plays.

Momentum grades evaluate a stock's price velocity and upward movement on a scale from A+ (strongest momentum) to F (weakest). Valuation grades measure equity prices against company fundamentals, with A+ representing the most undervalued stocks and F indicating the most overvalued.

Here is the list:

  1. Aspen Aerogels, Inc. (ASPN), Momentum: A+, Valuation: C-

  2. Flotek Industries, Inc. (FTK), Momentum: A+, Valuation: C-

  3. Kaiser Aluminum Corporation (KALU), Momentum: A+, Valuation: C-

  4. Koppers Holdings Inc. (KOP), Momentum: A+, Valuation: D

  5. Materion Corporation (MTRN), Momentum: A+, Valuation: F

  6. Myers Industries, Inc. (MYE), Momentum: A+, Valuation: D+

  7. Nucor Corporation (NUE), Momentum: A+, Valuation: D

  8. Perimeter Solutions, Inc. (PRM), Momentum: A+, Valuation: D

  9. Suncrete, Inc. (RMIX), Momentum: A+, Valuation: D-

  10. Steel Dynamics, Inc. (STLD), Momentum: A+, Valuation: D-
